newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Amcol ex-director cleared of one charge.
newsitem.headline: Amcol ex-director cleared of one charge.

text.p: Singapore businessman Peter Tay has been acquitted of a charge of retaining stolen property belonging to Amcol Holding Ltd's Mauritius project, but still faces a criminal conspiracy charge, a court official said on Wednesday.

"Tay has been acquitted of retaining stolen property related to Amcol's Mauritius project, but he still has to prove his innocence in another criminal conspiracy charge," an assistant for district judge Khoo Oon Soo told Reuters.
She said the charge was pending and a pre-trial conference would be held later on Wednesday, in which a hearing date for the defence would be called.

Tay faces a charge of conspiring with Ng Chee Kheng and Lloyd Lochra, former directors of property and trading firm Amcol, and others to cheat Amcol by getting it to invest US$39.6 million in a leisure and property project in Mauritius.

On Tuesday, after presentations of written submissions by the prosecution and defence in the subordinate courts, Khoo ruled that Tay had no case to answer on the charge of retaining US$300,000 in stolen property.
Amcol was put under judicial management last July after special auditors Price Waterhouse found the company had serious cash flow problems and difficulties meeting financial obligations.
Indonesia Sinar Mas Group agreed to buy Amcol in August and to inject US$2 billion in assets.
Amcol is being investigated by Singapore's Commercial Affairs Division regarding payments to various parties, including several Amcol directors.
